title: Deferred tool execution router — notes & proto
content:
Context:
This is a personal scratchpad for a lightweight router that accepts model responses with 'tool-calls' but defers the actual tool execution to a separate subsystem (execution-workers / external services). Goal: keep token latency fast for the user-facing generation path, avoid blocking on external tools, and allow controlled, observable orchestration of tool runs (retries, RBAC, cost tracking).

Why deferred?
- Some tools are slow (db searches, external API calls).
- We want the model to continue streaming partial responses while the tool runs asynchronously.
- Retry/circuit-breaker/fallback policies are easier when execution is a first-class ticket.

High-level flow (client perspective):
1) Client POSTs generate request with optional `tool_instructions` list.
2) Runtime returns streaming tokens immediately; whenever the model emits a tool invocation, the router creates an "execution ticket" and emits a compact tool-ref token to the client stream.
3) Execution workers pick tickets from queue and run the tool; results are attached to the ticket and can be fetched or pushed back to client via callback/webhook.
4) Model can be re-invoked with tool results by the runtime or client to continue the conversation (optionally automated).

Key primitives (API shapes) — canonical examples: 
Request: (client -> runtime/generate)
{
  "prompt": "Find the latest order for user 1234 and summarize",
  "stream": true,
  "tool_instructions": [
    {"id": "order_search", "type": "external_query", "security": "brokered", "timeout_ms": 5000, "spec": {"service": "orders.search", "params": {"user_id": "{{user_id}}"}}}
  ],
  "route_policy": "prefer-local-fast"
}

Router event sent in-stream when model calls a tool (compact token):
{
  "event": "TOOL_CALL",
  "ticket_id": "tkt_9f3a",
  "tool_ref": "order_search#v1",
  "meta": {"estimated_cost": "0.003", "lease_ttl_s": 30}
}

Execution ticket (internal object persisted to store):
{
  "ticket_id": "tkt_9f3a",
  "request_id": "req_abc",
  "tool_id": "order_search",
  "payload": {"user_id": "1234"},
  "state": "PENDING",
  "lease_expires_at": "2025-11-02T12:01:05Z",
  "attempts": 0,
  "idempotency_key": "ctx:xyz:call-1"
}

Execution result (worker -> router):
{
  "ticket_id": "tkt_9f3a",
  "status": "SUCCESS",
  "result_blob": {"orders": [{"id":"o-222", "amount": 142.30}]},
  "metrics": {"latency_ms": 4300, "external_calls": 1},
  "signature": "signed-by-runner-abc"
}

Router -> client follow-up push (webhook or websocket frame):
{
  "event": "TOOL_RESULT",
  "ticket_id": "tkt_9f3a",
  "result_summary": "found 1 order total $142.30",
  "continuation_hint": "call model with "PASTE_TOOL_RESULT:tkt_9f3a" to resume"
}

Config sketch (policy snippets):
- default_lease_ttl_s: 60
- max_retries: 2
- retry_backoff_ms: 500
- execution_priority: [local-cache, dedicated-workers, external-broker]
- cost_threshold_usd: 0.05  # if estimated > threshold, require explicit escalation
- fallback_behavior: ["model-only", "cached-preview", "degraded-summary"]

State machine (simplified ASCII):
PENDING -> RUNNING -> (SUCCESS | FAILED | TIMED_OUT) -> CLOSED
                        ^                 |
                        |                 v
                      RETRY <------------/
Notes: lease heartbeat from worker must renew; if lease expires, ticket goes back to PENDING and attempts++

Observability & telemetry to emit per ticket:
- ticket_created (ticket_id, tool_id, owner_request_id, est_cost, trace_id)
- ticket_acquired (worker_id, lease_id)
- ticket_completed (status, latency_ms, attempts, external_latency_ms)
- ticket_failed (error_class, http_code if applicable, circuit_breaker_state)
- ticket_requeued (reason)
Important: include model span id so we can correlate token latency to ticket lifecycle.

Edge cases / open problems (TODOs):
- Idempotency: if workers crash mid-execution, how do we ensure no double-effects? Use idempotency_key + runner-side checks; store opt-in "safe-mode" flags on tool definitions.
- Security boundary: some tools touch PII and must not be routable to untrusted workers. Need RBAC at ticket creation time and cryptographic envelope for payloads.
- Cost control: allow customers to opt-in to real-time cost veto (block tool call if est > threshold) vs async billing.
- Partial streaming + tool result injection: how to re-synchronize model context without blowing up token budget? Strategy: emit compact structured summary and optionally a persistent ticket ref; let client decide to re-run with full blob.
- Guaranteed delivery vs best-effort: for some tools (e.g., notifications) we need at-least-once semantics; for others we prefer best-effort. Ticket flags should capture this.

Developer UX:
- Minimal surface for SDK: on generate() return a stream of tokens and special ToolEvent objects. SDK should surface helper to fetch ticket result transparently.
- Admin console: list tickets, retry button, claim-to-debug (attach worker logs), and per-tool health.

Sample SDK ergonomics (pseudo-python):
for evt in client.generate(...):
    if isinstance(evt, ToolCall):
        ticket = evt.ticket_id
        res = client.fetch_tool_result(ticket, wait_ms=2000)  # returns None fast if not ready
        if res:
            client.continue_with_tool_result(ticket)

Operational metrics to track by SLA tier:
- p50/p95 time-to-ticket-ack (how quickly ticket persisted & queued)
- mean time to execution start (worker pick-up)
- ticket success rate and external failure breakdown
- fraction of model streams that emitted tool calls (for capacity planning)

Prototype checklist (short):
- [x] ticket store prototype (postgres) with simple TTL/lease pattern
- [x] runtime-insert compact token into stream on tool invocation (proto)
- [ ] worker pool prototype with async HTTP / gRPC runners and idempotency stub
- [ ] simple UI for ticket inspection and manual retry
- [ ] RBAC labels & encrypted payload envelopes

Unresolved UX decisions (notes to revisit):
- Should ticket creation be synchronous to the generate API call (i.e., block until ticket persisted)? I think yes for correctness but we should keep that persistence fast and local-only path.
- Do we expose full payloads to SDKs by default? Probably not; provide `fetch_tool_result` opt-in.

Reference links (internal):
- runtime PR with transient tokens: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/432
- spawn-workers prototype  (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/exec-workers/pull/19
- related design note: confluence://inference/def-tool-router

Open questions for next sync:
1) encryption-at-rest vs per-ticket envelope key rotation cadence?
2) default fallback policy for customer-free-tier vs enterprise?
3) how to charge for tool executions (prepay token units vs post-exec metering)?

Quick brainstorm: make a "preview" cache that stores first 100 bytes of result for immediate streaming; worker can attach a preview when ticket is created if an upstream cache can answer quickly (e.g., a fast local lookup). This can help reduce follow-ups.

---
Personal next steps: wire the ticket schema into local dev env, add small telemetry span id propagation to model->ticket events, and demo the SDK helper in next spike.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc intentionally terse; move to shared_drives/engineering once we have early prototype and API contract stable.
